figures.caption: Figure 1: An overview of FLOWDAGGER. A pre-trained generative policy πgp producing actions a is deployed with a human operator in the loop. When the operator intervenes, the corrective action a∗ is inverted back to a vector w∗ in the policy’s latent space. The resulting (s, w∗) pairs supervise a lightweight latent-space policy that adapts the policy without modifying the base model’s weights.
Table 1: Method comparison on MetaWorld with π0.5 as the base policy. The bottom rows give mean success rate and improvement over the frozen base. Best non-base method per row in bold.
Table 2: FlowDAgger across base-policy families, on a shared set of MetaWorld tasks. ∆ is the improvement over each frozen base.

Figure 6: Success rate vs. additional training episodes for FlowDAgger (green) and DSRL (purple) adapting a frozen diffusion policy on robomimic LIFT (state-only). Dashed line is the frozen base policy’s success rate. Single seed; each evaluation point averages 15 rollouts. FlowDAgger reaches ∼ 97% by episode 25; DSRL also climbs but plateaus around 80%.

Figure 5: Success rate vs. additional training episodes for FlowDAgger (green) and DSRL (purple) adapting frozen Gr00t N1.7 on LIBERO-90 task 57. Dashed line is the frozen base policy’s zeroshot success rate. Single seed; each evaluation point averages 15 rollouts. FlowDAgger matches the base policy after 5 episodes and saturates near 100% by episode 20; DSRL improves above base but plateaus around 70%.
Table 3: Prior preservation on π0.5: FlowDAgger holds the held-out tasks closest to the frozen base while gaining the most in-distribution. Bold: held-out scores within base noise or above.
